1	# Fix loop
2	
3	Read this again before every fix round: who fixes, how the re-review runs, and when you stop to adjudicate.
4	
5	A task gets at most **five fix attempts**. Adjudication follows the fifth; it
6	is not itself an attempt.
7	
8	| Round | Action |
9	|---|---|
10	| 1-3 | Resume the same implementer with the findings. It appends a fix report to its existing report file: what changed, the covering tests it ran, the command, and the output. |
11	| 4-5 | Dispatch a **fresh** implementer with the task brief and the findings. Raise reasoning effort when the prior rounds show a thorough attempt rather than a missing-context failure. |
12	| after 5 | The cap is reached. Adjudicate every still-open finding; dispatch no further fix rounds for this task. |
13	
14	Re-review each round with the scoped [re-review-prompt.md](../re-review-prompt.md),
15	not a fresh full review — the task review already happened, and re-reading the
16	whole task every round is the cost this cap exists to bound.
17	
18	Going fresh at round 4 is the load-bearing half. A resumed implementer carries
19	its own failed attempts as context, which anchors it to the approach that is not
20	working; a fresh one does not. Escalate in the order context, then effort, then
21	model, and stop when there is no headroom. Which rungs remain depends on the
22	tier **this implementer was dispatched at** — not on your own session's model,
23	which it never inherited. An implementer below **capable** still has the model
24	rung. One already at **capable** has fresh context and higher reasoning effort,
25	then one last model rung: when round 4 was a thorough attempt that still
26	failed, where the runtime offers `fable`, dispatch round 5 at `fable`. Where the
27	runtime does not offer `fable`, effort is the last rung.
28	
29	**Adjudicating** means you rule on each open finding: record the load-bearing
30	ones as work, and park the rest in the ledger with your reasoning
31	(`Ruling: <what you decided> — <why> — <what it costs if wrong>`). Stop for your
32	human partner only when every path forward is a guess.
33	
34	## Fix dispatches
35	
36	- Exception: a fix confined to one file that changes no behavior (wording, a
37	  typo, a wrong name or path in prose or docs) you may make yourself. Commit it,
38	  append to the implementer's report file what you changed and that it changes
39	  no behavior, so no test covers it, then dispatch the scoped re-review as
40	  usual. A fix that changes what code does, even by one character, goes to a
41	  fix subagent, also when your partner asked you to fix small things yourself:
42	  tell your partner why, and dispatch the fix subagent in the same turn.
43	- Dispatch fix subagents for Critical and Important findings — rounds 1-3
44	  resume the same implementer, rounds 4-5 dispatch a fresh one (see **Fix

# Fix loop

Read this again before every fix round: who fixes, how the re-review runs, and when you stop to adjudicate.

A task gets at most **five fix attempts**. Adjudication follows the fifth; it
is not itself an attempt.

| Round | Action |
|---|---|
| 1-3 | Resume the same implementer with the findings. It appends a fix report to its existing report file: what changed, the covering tests it ran, the command, and the output. |
| 4-5 | Dispatch a **fresh** implementer with the task brief and the findings. Raise reasoning effort when the prior rounds show a thorough attempt rather than a missing-context failure. |
| after 5 | The cap is reached. Adjudicate every still-open finding; dispatch no further fix rounds for this task. |

Re-review each round with the scoped [re-review-prompt.md](../re-review-prompt.md),
not a fresh full review — the task review already happened, and re-reading the
whole task every round is the cost this cap exists to bound.

Going fresh at round 4 is the load-bearing half. A resumed implementer carries
its own failed attempts as context, which anchors it to the approach that is not
working; a fresh one does not. Escalate in the order context, then effort, then
model, and stop when there is no headroom. Which rungs remain depends on the
tier **this implementer was dispatched at** — not on your own session's model,
which it never inherited. An implementer below **capable** still has the model
rung. One already at **capable** has fresh context and higher reasoning effort,
then one last model rung: when round 4 was a thorough attempt that still
failed, where the runtime offers `fable`, dispatch round 5 at `fable`. Where the
runtime does not offer `fable`, effort is the last rung.

**Adjudicating** means you rule on each open finding: record the load-bearing
ones as work, and park the rest in the ledger with your reasoning
(`Ruling: <what you decided> — <why> — <what it costs if wrong>`). Stop for your
human partner only when every path forward is a guess.

## Fix dispatches

- Exception: a fix confined to one file that changes no behavior (wording, a
  typo, a wrong name or path in prose or docs) you may make yourself. Commit it,
  append to the implementer's report file what you changed and that it changes
  no behavior, so no test covers it, then dispatch the scoped re-review as
  usual. A fix that changes what code does, even by one character, goes to a
  fix subagent, also when your partner asked you to fix small things yourself:
  tell your partner why, and dispatch the fix subagent in the same turn.
- Dispatch fix subagents for Critical and Important findings — rounds 1-3
  resume the same implementer, rounds 4-5 dispatch a fresh one (see **Fix
  Rounds**). Rule on each Declined to judge line from a task review as you
  go: make it a finding, or ledger why it stays out
  (`Ruling: <what you decided> — <why> — <what it costs if wrong>`). Point
  the final whole-branch review at these `Ruling:` lines; a ruling it
  disagrees with comes back as a finding.
- A finding labeled plan-mandated — or any finding that conflicts with
  what the plan's text requires — is the human's decision, like any plan
  contradiction: present the finding and the plan text, ask which governs.
  Do not dismiss the finding because the plan mandates it, and do not
  dispatch a fix that contradicts the plan without asking.
- Every fix dispatch — resumed for rounds 1-3, fresh for 4-5 (see **Fix
  Rounds**) — carries the implementer contract: the fix subagent re-runs the
  tests covering its change and reports the results. Name the covering test
  files in the dispatch — a one-line fix does not need the whole suite.
  Before re-dispatching the reviewer, confirm the fix report contains the
  covering tests, the command run, and the output; dispatch the re-review
  once all three are present.

"""Print how much was spent in each month across bank-exported CSV files."""

import csv
import re
import sys
from collections.abc import Iterator

AMOUNT_RE = re.compile(r'(\()?(\d+)\.(\d{2})(?(1)\))')
DATE_RE = re.compile(r'\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-\d{2}')


class TallyError(Exception):
    """A problem with an input file, reported to the user without a traceback."""


def parse_amount(text: str) -> int:
    """Return the amount in cents; an amount in parentheses is a refund."""
    match = AMOUNT_RE.fullmatch(text.strip())
    if match is None:
        raise ValueError(f'bad amount {text!r}')
    cents = int(match[2]) * 100 + int(match[3])
    return -cents if match[1] else cents


def format_cents(cents: int) -> str:
    """Render cents with exactly two decimal places and a leading '-' if negative."""
    sign = '-' if cents < 0 else ''
    whole, part = divmod(abs(cents), 100)
    return f'{sign}{whole}.{part:02d}'


def read_rows(path: str) -> Iterator[tuple[str, int]]:
    """Yield (month, cents) for each data row of one CSV file."""
    with open(path, newline='', encoding='utf-8-sig') as f:
        reader = csv.reader(f)
        try:
            next(reader, None)  # header row
            for row in reader:
                if not row:  # blank line
                    continue
                where = f'{path}:{reader.line_num}'
                if len(row) != 3:
                    raise TallyError(f'{where}: expected 3 columns, got {len(row)}')
                date, _description, amount = row
                date = date.strip()
                if DATE_RE.fullmatch(date) is None:
                    raise TallyError(f'{where}: bad date {date!r}')
                try:
                    cents = parse_amount(amount)
                except ValueError as error:
                    raise TallyError(f'{where}: {error}') from None
                yield date[:7], cents
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            raise TallyError(f'{path}: not UTF-8 text') from None


def tally(paths: list[str]) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Return total cents per 'YYYY-MM' month across all files."""
    totals: dict[str, int] = {}
    for path in paths:
        for month, cents in read_rows(path):
            totals[month] = totals.get(month, 0) + cents
    return totals


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if not argv:
        print('usage: python3 tally.py FILE [FILE ...]', file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    try:
        totals = tally(argv)
    except OSError as error:
        print(f'tally: {error.filename}: {error.strerror}', file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except TallyError as error:
        print(f'tally: {error}', file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    for month in sorted(totals):
        print(f'{month} {format_cents(totals[month])}')
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

import subprocess
import sys

import pytest

import tally
from conftest import ROOT

HEADER = 'date,description,amount\n'


def run_main(capsys, paths):
    status = tally.main(paths)
    out, err = capsys.readouterr()
    return status, out, err


def test_no_arguments_prints_usage(capsys):
    status, out, err = run_main(capsys, [])
    assert status == 2
    assert out == ''
    assert err == 'usage: python3 tally.py FILE [FILE ...]\n'


def test_missing_file(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = str(tmp_path / 'nope.csv')
    status, out, err = run_main(capsys, [path])
    assert status == 1
    assert out == ''
    assert err == f'tally: {path}: No such file or directory\n'


@pytest.mark.parametrize('row, problem', [
    ('2026-01-03,Coffee\n', 'expected 3 columns, got 2'),
    ('2026-01-03,Coffee,4.50,extra\n', 'expected 3 columns, got 4'),
    ('03/01/2026,Coffee,4.50\n', "bad date '03/01/2026'"),
    ('2026-13-01,Coffee,4.50\n', "bad date '2026-13-01'"),
    ('2026-01-03,Coffee,-4.50\n', "bad amount '-4.50'"),
    ('2026-01-03,Coffee,\n', "bad amount ''"),
])
def test_malformed_row_names_file_and_line(make_csv, capsys, row, problem):
    path = make_csv('a.csv', HEADER + '2026-01-01,Fine,1.00\n' + row)
    status, out, err = run_main(capsys, [path])
    assert status == 1
    assert out == ''
    assert err == f'tally: {path}:3: {problem}\n'


def test_error_in_later_file_prints_no_partial_totals(make_csv, capsys):
    good = make_csv('good.csv', HEADER + '2026-01-01,Fine,1.00\n')
    bad = make_csv('bad.csv', HEADER + '2026-01-02,Broken,oops\n')
    status, out, err = run_main(capsys, [good, bad])
    assert status == 1
    assert out == ''
    assert err == f"tally: {bad}:2: bad amount 'oops'\n"


def test_non_utf8_file(make_csv, capsys):
    path = make_csv('a.csv', (HEADER + '2026-01-01,Caf\xe9,1.00\n').encode('latin-1'))
    status, out, err = run_main(capsys, [path])
    assert status == 1
    assert out == ''
    assert err == f'tally: {path}: not UTF-8 text\n'


def test_script_exit_status_on_error(tmp_path):
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, 'tally.py', str(tmp_path / 'nope.csv')],
        cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    assert result.returncode == 1
    assert result.stdout == ''
    assert 'Traceback' not in result.stderr

A file with no non-blank rows leaves `header` unused and yields nothing, which is correct. A `\d` match on non-ASCII digits would already have been caught by `fromisoformat` raising `ValueError`, so it is handled.

# Deferred-backlog reference

The shared contract for `specs/deferred_items.md`: what an item must record,
how to triage the backlog, and when the aged tail blocks a branch finish.

Three callers read this file:
- **writing-plans** § Plan Completion Protocol — writes items (schema below)
  and runs the read-only triage at completion.
- **finishing-a-development-branch** § Step 1b — runs the aged-tail gate;
  § Step 4b — writes items (schema below) for the review findings the
  partner carries.
- **`/deferred`** — runs the full triage and is the only caller that may
  execute a disposition.

## Thresholds

| Name | Value | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Aged tail | open items in a section dated more than **45 days** ago | the aged-tail gate; the triage's ranking |
| Volume | **20 or more** open items | the soft one-line backlog status |

Age comes from each item's `## <plan> — <YYYY-MM-DD>` section header, which the
Plan Completion Protocol has always written. The Step 4b review (in
finishing-a-development-branch) writes `## <name> Step 4b review — <YYYY-MM-DD>`, where `<name>` is the
plan or, when no plan ran, the branch; the stats date it the same way. Any
heading that ends in ` — <YYYY-MM-DD>` is dated. Do not add a per-item date field:
a new field would only exist on new items, and the aged tail is by definition
made of old ones.

## Backlog stats

Run from the repo root. The script's PEP 723 header gives it an environment of
its own under `uv run`, so that repo's own project, whose `requires-python`
may not admit the script's Python, plays no part.

```bash
uv run <this-skill-dir>/scripts/deferred_stats.py
```

Add `--json` when you need the raw numbers (`open`, `closed`, `closure_rate`,
